title: Multi-agent Undercover Gaming: Hallucination Removal via Counterfactual Test for Multimodal Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2511.11182v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Hallucination continues to pose a major obstacle in the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). Although the Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) paradigm offers a promising solution by promoting consensus among multiple agents to enhance reliability, it relies on the unrealistic assumption that all debaters are rational and reflective, which is a condition that may not hold when agents themselves are prone to hallucinations. To address this gap, we introduce the Multi-agent Undercover Gaming (MUG) protocol, inspired by social deduction games like "Who is Undercover?". MUG reframes MAD as a process of detecting "undercover" agents (those suffering from hallucinations) by employing multimodal counterfactual tests. translated_title: 多智能体卧底游戏：通过反事实测试消除多模态推理中的幻觉
translated_abstract: 幻觉仍然是大型语言模型（LLM）推理能力面临的主要障碍。尽管多智能体辩论（MAD）范式通过促进多个智能体之间达成共识来提高可靠性，提供了一种有前景的解决方案，但它依赖于一个不切实际的假设，即所有辩论者都是理性和具备反思能力的——而当智能体自身容易产生幻觉时，这一条件可能并不成立。为了弥补这一不足，我们受“谁是卧底”等社交推理游戏的启发，提出了多智能体卧底游戏协议。MUG将多智能体辩论重新构建为一个检测“卧底”智能体（即受幻觉困扰的智能体）的过程，并采用多模态反事实测试来实现这一目标。具体而言，我们通过修改参考图像引入反事实证据，并观察智能体能否准确识别这些变化，从而为识别产生幻觉的智能体提供真实标准，并实现稳健的……
tldr: 受“谁是卧底”社交推理游戏启发，本文提出多智能体卧底游戏（MUG）协议，通过修改图像引入反事实证据来检测多智能体辩论中产生幻觉的“卧底”智能体并加以剔除，从而摆脱了传统MAD要求所有辩论者理性反思的不现实假设，提升多模态推理的可靠性。
en_tdlr: Inspired by the social deduction game "Who is Undercover?", this paper proposes the Multi-agent Undercover Gaming (MUG) protocol, which detects and removes hallucinating "undercover" agents in Multi-Agent Debate by introducing counterfactual evidence through image modifications, thereby relaxing the unrealistic assumption that all debaters are rational and reflective, and improving the reliability of multimodal reasoning.
